pattern: \(?POA\)? is (one|an HOA) too|property owners association[^.]{0,30} is (one|an HOA) too
struck: A property owners association (POA) is one too.
use: A property owners association (POA) that meets that test is one too.

struck: Any group that runs a planned neighborhood or a condo regime, where a recorded declaration makes every owner pay assessments, is a "homeowners association" under the state's HOA Act.
use: Any group that runs a planned neighborhood or a condo regime, where a recorded declaration makes every owner pay assessments, is a "homeowners association" under the state's HOA Act, except a timeshare plan.

struck: Voluntary or mandatory is set by the documents, not the name.
use: The recorded documents decide whether dues are voluntary or mandatory, not the name.

struck: Before a contract, a seller in any association gives the buyer one disclosure addendum.
use: Before a contract, the seller of a home in any kind of association gives the buyer the state's disclosure addendum, unless the sale is exempt (a new home never lived in, a foreclosure or court sale, an auction, or both sides agree in writing to skip it).

struck: That is why the condo fee here is called a regime fee, and why the deed gives a condo away.
use: A condo regime's name in its master deed must end in "Horizontal Property Regime", and a deed may describe a unit by its number "in Horizontal Property Regime".

struck: The common parts can never be split up or sold off by one owner.
use: The common parts stay undivided; no owner can force them to be split up, and selling a unit sells its share with it.

struck: A condo owner owns the unit outright, plus a share of everything held in common.
use: A condo owner owns the unit alone, plus a share of everything held in common.

struck: If a neighbor does not pay, the building cannot be sold for their tax.
use: If a neighbor does not pay, a tax sale cannot take your unit while your own taxes are paid.

struck: Fannie Mae requires a review of the project before a loan on a unit in a condo building of more than ten units.
use: Fannie Mae requires a project review for an attached condo unit in a project of more than ten units, or of five to ten units that is part of a larger development or master association.
